question: ADR-0002 still has no corruption clause for the shared context.db. On SQLITE_CORRUPT, which process renames the file aside, and what do other open writer handles do next: retry-reopen or hard-fail and tell the agent to restart?
answer: ADR-0002 does not state this; it names no corruption rule at all (engine, timeout, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, retention — nothing on SQLITE_CORRUPT). This is a confirmed, repeated gap: BOTTLENECKS-r3 line 22-24, REVIEW-r2 ADR-0002:17, and BOTTLENECKS-r4 #2 / REVIEW-r4a #7 all flag it as a blocker and all ask for the same two unanswered sub-questions this ticket raises (who renames, what do other writers do). DECISIONS-r3 and OWNER-QUESTIONS-r3 record no answer either. v1's matching code (git archaeology below) cannot be ported as-is because v1 never had this multi-writer shape: each v1 handle (SessionDB/ContentStore) owned its own private DB file, so there was only ever one writer to heal. a5c449df's withRetry caught SQLITE_CORRUPT on the SAME handle that hit the error, healed or renamed in place, then retried that same call locally - it never had to coordinate with other open handles on the same file, because none existed. v2's ADR-0002 model puts 4+ agents/worktrees/sessions on one shared context.db, so a straight port leaves the 'what do the other handles do' question unanswered, exactly as BOTTLENECKS-r4 #2 and REVIEW-r4a #57 say.
evidence: docs/v2/adr/0002-single-db-git-distribution.md (Decision: engine/timeout/BEGIN IMMEDIATE/distribution/migration — no corruption clause); docs/v2/review/BOTTLENECKS-r3.md:22-24; docs/v2/review/REVIEW-r2.md:40 (ADR-0002:17 blocker row); docs/v2/review/BOTTLENECKS-r4.md:12-17 (#2, storage, BLOCKER); docs/v2/review/REVIEW-r4a.md:19,121 (#7, #57); docs/v2/review/ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r4.md:194,350 (issue #867, #871, both needs-decision/closed-by-design-with-open-question).

finding.claim: ADR-0002's write-rules section (engine, timeout, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, chunked writes, no retry loop) has no SQLITE_CORRUPT clause for the one shared context.db, so the DB-open code path has no rule to implement for the multi-writer case BOTTLENECKS-r4 #2 names.
finding.evidence: docs/v2/adr/0002-single-db-git-distribution.md lines 17-24 cover engine/timeout/BEGIN IMMEDIATE/chunking/retry only; docs/v2/review/BOTTLENECKS-r4.md:15-17 states v1's matching fix (commit 9e246a8e, and the a5c449df/50aafdce chain) only ever had one writer per DB file, so it does not map onto a file shared by many open handles; no doc states which process renames the file or what the other open handles do after the rename.
finding.fix: Add a Corruption subsection to ADR-0002 Decision: (1) name the one process allowed to rename context.db aside on SQLITE_CORRUPT - recommend the 'last writer' role already defined for the WAL checkpoint in Q6, since that is the only existing single-owner designation in the doc; (2) state that it is rename-only, never delete (ADR-0008/BOTTLENECKS-r3 already rule out delete since there is no ephemeral store left); (3) state explicitly what every OTHER open writer handle does once its path is renamed out from under it - recommend hard-fail on the next write with a clear error naming ctx_doctor's fix action, not a silent retry-reopen, since 'no fallback chains' (owner decision, README §22) and 'no retry loop' (ADR-0002 line 24) already rule out an automatic reopen loop; a reopen would be exactly that retry loop under a different name.

recommendation: Given the existing owner decisions (no fallback chains, no retry loop, rename-only no delete), the consistent answer is: the last-writer role (Q6) does the rename; every other open writer hard-fails on its next operation against the now-missing path and surfaces an error that names ctx_doctor's fix step, telling the agent/session to restart - not an automatic retry-reopen, since that would silently reintroduce the retry loop the ADR already forbids. This is a recommendation, not a documented decision - the owner should confirm it and add it to ADR-0002.
